module: Gamepad/keyboard 'code' detector: at 30 Hz it watches the inputs (throttle, brake, steering left/right, clutch, parking brake), builds a string of the last 16 presses and calls a callback when the end of the string matches a registered sequence (8 to 16 characters). Used for easter eggs.
usage:
-- letters: u throttle, d brake, l left, r right, a clutch, b parking brake
extensions.inputAnalyzer.registerInputString('uuddlrlrab', function(s) print('code!') end)
notes: Each new press (transition from false to true above 0.01) appends its letter to the string. The string is truncated by one character when it exceeds 16.
The inputs read are electrics.values.throttle_input, brake_input, steering_input (l = negative part, r = positive part), clutch_input and parkingbrake_input.
registerInputString ignores strings shorter than 8 or longer than 16 characters.
Anomaly: the duplicate test in registerInputString compares `v.string == string` (the string library) instead of `str`: it is never true, so the same code can be registered several times.
Anomaly: the parameter of unregisterInputString is named `string` and shadows the string library (no consequence here).
If one of the electrics keys read is nil, abs(nil) raises an error; they are normally initialized by the inputs.

updateGFX.desc: Called every frame: runs the input analysis at 30 Hz (no-op when no code is registered after a (un)register).

registerInputString.desc: Registers a sequence to detect and the callback called with the current string when it is entered.

str.desc: Sequence of 8 to 16 letters among u, d, l, r, a, b.

unregisterInputString.desc: Removes a registered sequence (same string and same callback); enables/disables updateGFX depending on whether sequences remain.
